# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 88 (Bi-Vb Pc88)

**Title (English, from literature):** Bathing in scents and colors

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 88 (*Gandhavaṇṇaka*, "Bathing in scents and colors") is a monastic rule of expiation (*pācittiya*) in the Vinaya Piṭaka for Buddhist nuns. The rule establishes that a nun who bathes using scents, perfumed powders, or colorings commits an offense requiring confession [Hüsken 1997]. As Ute Hüsken notes, while monks were permitted certain scented clays in the context of bathhouse use, nuns were barred from bathhouses entirely; under this regulation (*Pāc 88 (N)*), nuns are prohibited from using powders and scented clay, leaving them permitted only red powder from rice husks, natural unperfumed clay, and unperfumed sesame paste as bathing agents [Hüsken 1997]. An English translation of the rule has been published by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

  DharmaNexus machine analysis similarly identifies its strongest internal text reuse with Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 89 (§0.1–2.2.4 matching §0.1–2.2.5), alongside standard Vinaya formulas shared with Pācittiyas 87, 84, and 50 [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language matches, DharmaNexus automatically aligns the text with the Tibetan *Āryasarvāstivādimūlabhikṣuṇīpratimokṣasūtravṛtti* (D4112) and the Sanskrit *Carmavastu* [DharmaNexus].
